deep.reconstruction:
This page is not mathematics. It is a postage (Porto) ledger for 1816, kept in a small account book and continuing the previous page. Each line records a date, the correspondent and an amount of postage, in Gute Groschen and Pfennig.

Layout of the left half (January to early April 1816):
- Column 1: day of the month.
- Column 2: the name of the correspondent from whom a letter arrived, or to whom one was sent. Names include von Lindenau, Nicolai, von Wehrs, Olbers, Bode, Littrow, Sander, Huber, v. Buquoy, Bessel, Hofer, Gerling, Möbius, Repsold, Fleischer, Reichenbach, Baumann, v. Zimmermann, Encke and the Curatorium.
- Column 3: a second name, probably the other direction of correspondence (letters sent).
- Final columns: the porto amount.
- One special item reads 'Bücherporto v. Leipzig', postage on books from Leipzig, at 30 gr 9 pf.

Layout of the right half (April to October 1816):
- Entries for Mollweide, Lindenau, Wehrs and Schumacher, then a ruled subtotal of 85 gr 11 pf.
- An item 'Porto während der Reise' (postage during the journey) to 23 May: Braunschweig, Hannover, Coburg. This is Gauss's spring 1816 trip to Bavaria, to Reichenbach and Utzschneider about instruments.
- Further letters (Wehrs, Lindenau, Gerling, Hofer, Bessel, Reichenbach) and a ruled total of 145 gr 2 pf, with a side figure '1 11'.
- Then July to September (Lindenau, Olbers, Schmidt/Schumacher, Mollweide, Müller, Hofer, Augsburg, Littrow, Nicolai, Reichenbach/Bode, Seeber, Fleischer, Utzschneider/Gerling) and a total written '2 | 17.2', i.e. 2 Thaler 17 gr 2 pf.
- The last entries (October: Wehrs, Ahrentschildt) are repeated at the top of the next page under 'An Breithaupt zu bezahl'.

The only 'computation' on the page is adding money amounts. The units are 1 Thaler = 24 gute Groschen and 1 Groschen = 12 Pfennig.

Total check A, reconstructed by me: the block 38gr11 + 11gr3 + 3gr2 + 86gr4 + 4gr0 + 1gr6 comes to 1742 pf = 145 gr 2 pf. This matches the written total; the struck '0 2' is excluded.

Total check B, also mine: the July–September block 4gr2 + 3gr4 + 1gr8 + 0gr2 + 3gr6 + 3gr4 + 26gr2 + 3gr4 + 3gr0 + 3gr0 + 3gr4 + 3gr6 + 3gr6 + 3gr2 comes to 782 pf = 65 gr 2 pf. That equals 2 Thaler 17 gr 2 pf, as written; the struck '2 11' is excluded.

The first subtotal of 85 gr 11 pf could not be reproduced from the visible left-column figures alone. It may involve amounts from the previous page or only part of the column.
errors: No arithmetic errors detected in the two totals that could be checked: 145 gr 2 pf and 2 Th 17 gr 2 pf.
The subtotal 85 gr 11 pf does not equal the sum of all visible left-column amounts on this page (those sum to more). Its scope is unclear, so this is not counted as an error.

results.what: Household/office ledger of postage paid on scientific correspondence in 1816, with running totals in Thaler/Groschen/Pfennig
results.modern_name: Bookkeeping; sums in a mixed-radix currency (24 gr = 1 Th, 12 pf = 1 gr)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine postage account with no mathematical content. Its value is historical only: it documents Gauss's 1816 correspondence network (Olbers, Bessel, Lindenau, Gerling, Schumacher, Encke, Möbius, Reichenbach, Utzschneider, Repsold) and the postage during his 1816 Bavarian journey, all of which is already well documented.

checkable.asserts: The second block sums to the written total of 145 gr 2 pf (12 pf per gr).
The July–September block sums to 2 Thaler 17 gr 2 pf (24 gr per Thaler, 12 pf per gr).

transcription_corrections: The amounts are postage in Gute Groschen and Pfennig, not mathematical quantities; the right-hand '2 | 17.2' should be read as 2 Thaler 17 gr 2 pf.
'Portowährend der Reise' should read 'Porto während der Reise'.
'Olbers Encny[?]' is unclear on the image; the second word may be 'Encke' or a place name, uncertain.

Around Aug 24 the image shows '3 —' and '3 4' stacked. The transcription's separate entries 3—, 3—, 3 4, 3 6, 3 6 are consistent with the total 2 Th 17 gr 2 pf, so both stacked figures are real entries.
